sentences.text:
Rakesh Singh Gurjar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31
March, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:10725
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajesh Kumar Gupta
 On The 31st Of March, 2026
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 8940 of 2026
 Rakesh Singh Gurjar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Mr. Sankalp Sharma - Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. Atul Kumar Sharma - Govt. Advocate for respondent
 Order
This is the third application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. for grant of bail.
The applicant has been arrested in connection with Crime No.607/2024 registered at Police Station - City Kotwali, District - Morena (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
His earlier both applications were dismissed on merit.

2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation is that, through a conspiracy, a forged registered sale deed MP 2579202A11271083 was executed between the complainant and other co-accused persons,
in which, the present applicant signed the said sale deed as a consenting party, on the basis of which, the aforesaid FIR was registered against the present applicant and the other co-accused persons.

3. Counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:10725 2 MCRC-8940-2026 falsely been implicated in the present matter.

It is further submitted that apart from the signature of the present applicant on the registered sale deed as a consenting party, there is no other material to connect the present applicant with the present crime.
It is further argued that the applicant is not a beneficiary in the said case, nor did he receive any money.
At best, this is a case of a civil nature that has been given the color of a criminal case.
The present applicant is not a part of any conspiracy or misdeed in the sale transaction of the disputed land.

Counsel for the applicant has placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mihir Rajesh Shah Vs. State of Maharashtra, wherein, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under:
Rakesh Singh Gurjar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167516451/
1 "Article 22 of the Constitution of India further strengthens the protection of personal liberty of a person by providing that a person arrested must be informed of the grounds of his arrest at the earliest and should not be detained without informing him of such grounds.

sentences.text:
Article 22 reads as follow:
"22. Protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.- (1) No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest nor shall he be denied the right to consult, and to be defended by, a legal practitioner of his choice."

(2) Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within a period of twenty- four hours of such arrest excluding the time necessary for the journey from the place of arrest to the court of the magistrate and no such person shall be detained in custody beyond the said period without the authority of a magistrate.

xxx (5) When any person is detained in pursuance of an order made under any law providing for preventive detention, the authority making the order shall, as soon as may be, communicate to such NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10725 3 MCRC-8940-2026 person the grounds on which the order has been made and shall afford him the earliest opportunity of making a representation against the order...."

19 . The Constitutional safeguard provided under Article 22 of the Constitution of India has been effectuated by the legislature by incorporating Section 50 of CrPC 1973 (now Section 47 of BNSS 2023) which puts into force the procedural mandate providing for the protection of the personal liberty of the person so arrested.
Section 47 of BNSS 2023 casts a duty on the police officer or other person arresting any person without a warrant shall communicate him the grounds of arrest."

In light of the aforesaid judgment, it is mandatory for the Police Authorities to establish grounds for arresting the accused person; however, in the present case, such grounds are absent, and therefore,
the applicant deserves the grant of bail.
There is no criminal antecedent against the present applicant.
Investigation is complete, therefore, custodial interrogation is no longer required.
Applicant is a permanent resident of District Gwalior (M.P.), therefore, there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
Applicant undertakes to cooperate in trial as well as the investigation and would make himself available as and when required.
Under these grounds, counsel prayed for bail.

4. Per contra, Counsel for the Respondent/State and Counsel for the Complainant vehemently opposed the bail application, stating that there is sufficient material available on record to involve the present applicant in the alleged crime.
Counsel for the Respondent/Complainant has drawn the attention of this Court to the sale deed, where the name of the present applicant is mentioned as consenting party.
It is further submitted that he was aware of the fact regarding the fake execution of the sale deed.
In such NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:10725 4 MCRC-8940-2026 circumstances, they prayed for the dismissal of this bail application.

sentences.text: 5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and upon perusal of the case diary, it appears that there is no material or substantial change in circumstances subsequent to the dismissal of the earlier bail application that would warrant reconsideration or a different view from that already taken by this Court.
The judgment relied upon by learned counsel for the applicant is not applicable to the factual matrix of the present case.

7. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case, as well as the nature of allegations against the present applicant and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the matter, this Court is of the view that no ground for grant of bail is made out at this stage.
Therefore, the application is dismissed.

(RAJESH KUMAR GUPTA ) JUDGE (LJ*)
